title: Add evidence ledger (KMS-anchored audit) and RBAC timebox enforcement
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation: Customers in regulated industries asked for a tamper-evident, compact audit store that can be cryptographically anchored to a KMS-backed signature and queried with efficient proofs. Current audit forwarding meets retention needs but lacks a concise, queryable index and timeboxed RBAC controls for short-lived operator delegations. This PR introduces an "evidence ledger" service that: 1) batches audit events into compact attestation envelopes anchored by a KMS attestation call, 2) maintains a small append-only index optimized for retrospective queries (compact bloom + chunked hashes), and 3) enforces RBAC timebox constraints (time-limited delegation grants and per-delegation quotas) at the policy layer.

What this changes: Implementation includes a new evidence ledger component (pkg/audit/ledger) that accepts audit events, compacts them into an envelope, and calls the KMS attest endpoint to produce an anchor token. A lightweight indexer (pkg/audit/indexer) stores chunk hashes and a bloom summary allowing fast existence checks without full scan. RBAC changes add a timebox policy (pkg/rbac/timebox) which integrates into the decision path; operator tokens can be minted with explicit TTLs and delegation quotas. We also add a retrospective attestation API (api/v1/evidence) that returns an attestation bundle and an index proof suitable for downstream compliance tooling.

Backward compatibility and migration: Existing audit-forwarding continues unchanged. The evidence ledger runs as an opt-in service behind a feature flag (feature.audit.evidence_ledger = off by default). We provide a one-time migration tool (tools/audit/migrate_to_ledger) to convert recent audit files into the ledger envelopes; migration is recommended for accounts enabling Evidence Ledger. RBAC timebox enforcement is additive: policies without timebox fields behave as before.

Security considerations: The KMS attestation requests are rate-limited and use operator-scoped credentials. Anchors include an HMAC over the envelope and a KMS-signed timestamp token to prevent replay. We added unit tests that simulate KMS failures and exercise fallback retry/backoff. The ledger persists only digests + compact metadata; raw events remain in existing audit storage unless the customer opts into envelope-only retention (documented).

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover ledger envelope composition, index bloom false-positive bounds, and policy evaluation with timeboxes. Integration tests exercise KMS attestation (using a KMS test double) and the retrospective API. Initial integration runs were flaky on the KMS test double (race in the mock); fixed by stubbing clock advancement and stabilizing async flush path.

Rollout plan: Feature flag gated rollout: enable in internal staging -> canary (10% tenant sample) -> wide. Metrics: anchor_latency_ms, anchor_error_rate, index_bloom_fp_rate, timebox_enforcement_denials. We added dashboard tiles in observability package for the canary.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3289)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Feature flag + migration tool included
- [x] Compliance docs updated (docs/compliance/evidence-ledger.md)
- [x] SRE runbook excerpt + dashboard (observability/dashboards/evidence-ledger.json)

Notes for reviewers: look closely at the policy decision path change in pkg/rbac/decision.go — I had to introduce a light-weight pre-check to short-circuit obvious denials before full policy evaluation to keep latency within SLOs. Also review the compact bloom parameters in indexer.go (we tuned for typical tenant sizes). For customers who opt into envelope-only retention we added an explicit consent flow; that path requires legal sign-off before enabling in production.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in Evidence Ledger: a KMS-anchored, tamper-evident audit envelope service and a RBAC timebox policy for short-lived delegation grants. Feature is behind a feature flag and includes a migration utility. Metrics and dashboards added for rollout.
